# The Tale of the First Echo

Long ago, when the world was young and silence ruled the mountains, there lived a lonely giant named Oron. He was the last of his kind, wandering the peaks with no one to speak to.

One day, Oron climbed the highest mountain and shouted his name into the vast emptiness, hoping someone, somewhere, might hear him. But only silence answered.

Heartbroken, he cried out again and again, his voice growing hoarse. "Is anyone there? Will I be alone forever?"

The Mountain Spirit, who had watched Oron for years, took pity on him. She could not create another giant, but she could give him something precious. She wove a spell into the mountain walls, capturing fragments of Oron's voice and teaching the stones to remember.

When Oron next called out, the mountains called back—not with new words, but with his own, repeated and returned to him.

Oron wept with joy. Though the echo was only his own voice, it was still companionship. He was no longer speaking into nothingness.

From that day forward, the mountains have remembered every voice spoken to them, offering back our own words as comfort—a reminder that we are heard, even when we feel most alone.
